ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, $AB\parallel CD\parallel EF$. If $AC: CE = 2: 3$ and $BF = 10$, what is the length of the line segment $DF$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
Solution: Since $AB\parallel CD\parallel EF$,\\
hence $\frac{BD}{DF}=\frac{AC}{CE} = \frac{2}{3}$,\\
Since $BF=10$,\\
thus $DF=10 \times \frac{3}{5} = \boxed{6}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there are three horizontal parallel lines, cut by two oblique lines on the left and right. The left oblique line intersects the three parallel lines from top to bottom at A, C, E in order; the right oblique line intersects the three parallel lines from top to bottom at B, D, F in order. Therefore AC and CE are the two segments of the left transversal between adjacent parallel lines, and BD and DF are the two segments of the right transversal between the corresponding adjacent parallel lines. Reasoning: From the meaning of the problem, AB ∥ CD ∥ EF, and the corresponding segments obtained when parallel lines cut two transversals are proportional, so BD:DF = AC:CE = 2:3. Also BF = BD + DF = 10, the total number of proportional parts is 2 + 3 = 5, and the length of each part is 10 ÷ 5 = 2. Therefore DF corresponds to 3 parts, DF = 3 × 2 = 6.

method.method_draft: First read the diagram: the three parallel horizontal lines create the same top-to-middle-to-bottom division on both slanted sides, with A,C,E on the left side and B,D,F on the right side. From the text, AC:CE = 2:3, so C is 2/(2+3) = 2/5 of the way from A to E. Because CD is parallel to AB and EF, the middle parallel hits the right transversal at the same fractional position: D is 2/5 of the way from B to F.
